newsitem.title: USA: Texas executes killer of waitress.
newsitem.headline: Texas executes killer of waitress.

text.p: A truck driver convicted of raping and strangling a 20-year-old cocktail waitress in 1985 was executed Monday by lethal injection in a Texas prison.
Benjamin Boyle, 53, died seven minutes after receiving a dose of lethal chemicals in his arm, Texas Department of Corrections spokesman David Nunnelee said.
"He just shook his head 'no' when asked if he had a last statement. He took a deep breath and that was it," Nunnelee said.
Boyle had no visitors on his last day and ordered a double-meat cheeseburger, french fries and a soft drink for his last meal, Nunnelee said.
Boyle, who was from Kiowa County, Oklahoma, was found guilty of raping and killing Gail Smith after she hitched a ride in his truck in October 1985 outside Fort Worth, Texas.

Police said Smith's hands and feet were bound by duct tape and she was strangled with a necktie. Her body, which showed evidence of sexual assault, was found off a highway near the city of Amarillo in the Texas Panhandle.
Boyle was the sixth person executed in Texas this year and the 114th since the state reinstated the death penalty in 1982.
Texas has executed more people than any other state since the United States restored capital punishment in 1976.
